brief.headline: Asian Markets Open Lower Following Severe Wall Street Tech Sell-Off; India Cues Mixed
brief.summary: Asian equities fell sharply following a steep tech sell-off on Wall Street, with the Nasdaq entering a bear market amid growing concerns over AI spending. Meanwhile, domestic sentiment remains supported by strong corporate earnings and robust banking momentum, though rising metal and energy import bills require close monitoring.

takeaways.text: Tata Steel announced a ₹28,000 crore deal to transfer its tubes business and divest its entire stake in Tata Steel Colors to APL Apollo Tubes.
India's oil and gas import bill surged 60% year-on-year to $16 billion in October as Brent crude prices nearly doubled.
Wall Street suffered its worst week since the Covid-19 crisis, with the Nasdaq plunging into a bear market amid a broader sell-off in AI stocks.
Anthropic made its public market debut on the Nasdaq at a massive $1.5 trillion valuation, capping an explosive growth period for the AI startup.
RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra is set to meet NBFC and MFI executives to discuss rural lending, microfinance regulations, and gold loan delinquencies.

sections.india: Indian markets enter the week following a fourth consecutive winning week for the Nifty 50, led by strong banking and hospital stocks. Key corporate developments include Tata Steel's ₹28,000 crore asset transfer deal with APL Apollo Tubes and AU Small Finance Bank preparing for a ₹5,000 crore QIP. However, macroeconomic headwinds persist as India's net oil and gas import bill jumped 60% in October alongside crashing precious metal prices.
sections.world: Global markets are under heavy pressure following a brutal sell-off on Wall Street, where the Nasdaq tumbled into a bear market and the S&P 500 dropped 3.70%. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned that the Federal Reserve risks overtightening, while regional inflation pressures continue to challenge central banks in Switzerland and Japan. Asian indices followed suit, with Nikkei 225 down 5.06% and Hang Seng lower by 1.89%.
sections.tech: The technology sector faces intense scrutiny following the historic $1.5 trillion market debut of AI lab Anthropic and ongoing governance turmoil at Nvidia. Amazon is reportedly closing in on a $7.5 billion acquisition of AI startup Decart to compete in cloud computing. Meanwhile, US regulatory bodies are investigating Nvidia's accounting practices and chip sales to China.
